title: New Drug Offers Hope for Patients with Pancreatic Cancer
subtitle: The FDA has approved a groundbreaking treatment that helps patients live longer with fewer side effects.

summary.en: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has officially approved a new drug called daraxonrasib for advanced pancreatic cancer. This daily pill targets a specific protein that helps tumors grow, which was previously thought to be impossible to treat. Clinical studies show that patients taking the drug lived nearly twice as long as those on traditional chemotherapy. While the medicine is not a cure, doctors see it as a significant step forward in cancer treatment. The drug will be sold under the brand name Rasonque.
summary.zh: 美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）已正式核准一款名為 daraxonrasib 的新藥，用於治療晚期胰臟癌。這款每日服用的口服藥針對一種先前被認為無法治療、且有助於腫瘤生長的特定蛋白質。臨床研究顯示，服用該藥物的患者存活時間幾乎是接受傳統化學治療患者的兩倍。雖然該藥物並非治癒良方，但醫生將其視為癌症治療的一大進步。該藥物將以 Rasonque 的品牌名稱販售。

paragraphs.en: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has officially approved a new, groundbreaking drug for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer. This decision, announced on Wednesday, marks an important moment in the fight against one of the deadliest forms of cancer. The new medicine, called daraxonrasib, is a daily pill that targets a specific protein that helps tumors grow. For many years, scientists believed this protein was impossible to treat, but this new approach has finally proven successful.
paragraphs.zh: 美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）已正式核准一款針對晚期胰臟癌患者的突破性新藥。這項於週三宣布的決定，標誌著對抗此類最致命癌症之一的過程中，邁出了重要的一步。這款名為 daraxonrasib 的新藥為每日服用一次的口服藥，其作用目標是一種有助於腫瘤生長的特定蛋白質。多年來，科學家一直認為這種蛋白質無法透過藥物治療，但這種新方法最終證明是成功的。

paragraphs.en: According to NPR Health, the FDA gave the drug an expedited approval, meaning it was approved more than six months ahead of the original target date. The agency’s acting commissioner, Kyle Diamantas, stated that the FDA has a duty to provide new treatments to patients as quickly as possible. This approval follows a period of high public interest, especially after former Senator Ben Sasse shared his own positive experience with the drug on television earlier this year. Because of this interest, the FDA had already allowed some patients to access the drug before it was officially approved.
paragraphs.zh: 根據美國公共廣播電台（NPR）健康頻道的報導，食品藥物管理局對該藥物採取了加速審核程序，這意味著它比原定目標日期提前了超過六個月獲得核准。該機構代理局長凱爾·迪亞曼塔斯（Kyle Diamantas）表示，食品藥物管理局有責任盡快為患者提供新的治療方法。此次核准是在公眾高度關注下進行的，特別是在前參議員班·薩斯（Ben Sasse）今年稍早於電視上分享他服用該藥物的正面經驗之後。由於這種關注，食品藥物管理局先前已允許部分患者在正式核准前取得該藥物。

paragraphs.en: Pancreatic cancer is notoriously difficult to treat because it is often not found until it has already started to spread to other organs. The American Cancer Society estimates that there will be about 67,000 new cases in the United States this year, with more than 52,000 people expected to die from the disease. The survival rate for this cancer is very low, with only about 13% of patients living for five years after diagnosis. Because of these grim statistics, medical experts have been looking for new ways to fight the disease for decades.
paragraphs.zh: 胰臟癌因通常在擴散至其他器官後才被發現，因此以難以治療著稱。美國癌症協會（American Cancer Society）估計，今年美國將新增約六萬七千名病例，預計有超過五萬兩千人會死於此疾病。這種癌症的存活率極低，僅約百分之十三的患者在確診後能存活五年。由於這些嚴峻的統計數據，醫學專家數十年來一直在尋找對抗該疾病的新方法。

paragraphs.en: The new drug works by targeting mutations in the RAS gene family, which normally controls how cells grow. In more than 90% of pancreatic cancer cases, these mutations fuel the growth of tumors. Revolution Medicines, the company that makes the drug, will sell it under the brand name Rasonque. The company announced that a one-month supply of the medication will cost approximately $39,800. While the price is high, the results from clinical trials have been very encouraging for both doctors and patients.
paragraphs.zh: 這款新藥的作用機制是針對 RAS 基因家族的突變，該基因通常負責控制細胞生長。在超過百分之九十的胰臟癌病例中，這些突變會助長腫瘤的生長。負責製造該藥物的藥廠 Revolution Medicines 將以 Rasonque 的品牌名稱販售。該公司宣布，一個月份的藥量費用約為三萬九千八百美元。儘管價格高昂，但臨床試驗的結果對醫生和患者而言都非常令人振奮。

paragraphs.en: In a study involving 500 patients whose cancer had continued to spread despite other treatments, those taking the new drug lived for a median of 13.2 months. In comparison, patients who received traditional chemotherapy lived for only 6.7 months. This means the new treatment nearly doubled the survival time for patients in the study. Furthermore, patients taking the pill reported fewer severe side effects than those on chemotherapy, though they did experience issues such as skin rashes, mouth sores, and digestive problems.
paragraphs.zh: 在一項涉及五百名儘管接受其他治療但癌症仍持續擴散的患者研究中，服用該新藥的患者中位存活期為十三點二個月。相比之下，接受傳統化學治療的患者僅存活了六點七個月。這意味著新療法使研究中患者的存活時間幾乎增加了一倍。此外，服用該藥物的患者報告的嚴重副作用比化學治療患者少，儘管他們確實經歷了皮膚紅疹、口腔潰瘍和消化問題等症狀。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Andrew Coveler of the Fred Hutch Cancer Center noted that while this medicine is not a cure, it represents a significant improvement in care. He described the approval as one of the most anticipated events in the field of cancer research. Doctors are hopeful that this success will lead to more options for other types of cancer in the future. Because the drug uses a special technology that acts like a "molecular glue" to bind with cancer proteins, researchers believe it could be adapted to treat other diseases, including lung cancer.
paragraphs.zh: 弗雷德·哈欽森癌症中心（Fred Hutch Cancer Center）的安德魯·科維勒（Andrew Coveler）醫師指出，雖然這種藥物並非治癒良方，但它代表了照護上的重大進步。他將此次核准描述為癌症研究領域中最受期待的事件之一。醫生們希望這一成功將在未來為其他類型的癌症帶來更多選擇。由於該藥物使用了一種特殊的技術，其作用如同「分子膠水」與癌症蛋白質結合，研究人員認為它未來可能經過調整後用於治療其他疾病，包括肺癌。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, many in the medical community believe this is just the beginning. Dr. Pashtoon Kasi of City of Hope Orange County said that this approval has opened doors for many other companies. He expects that there will be many more clinical trials—research studies to test if a new treatment works—looking at this same approach for different types of tumors. As researchers continue to study this technology, the hope is that it will provide even more effective ways to help patients who have run out of other treatment options. For now, the approval of Rasonque provides a new, meaningful tool for doctors and a new sense of hope for families facing a difficult diagnosis.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，醫學界許多人認為這僅僅是個開始。希望之城橘郡分院（City of Hope Orange County）的帕什通·卡西（Pashtoon Kasi）醫師表示，這項核准為許多其他公司開啟了大門。他預計未來將會有更多臨床試驗——即測試新療法是否有效的科學研究——針對不同類型的腫瘤探討相同的方法。隨著研究人員持續研究這項技術，人們希望它能為那些已無其他治療選擇的患者提供更有效的途徑。目前，Rasonque 的核准為醫生提供了一種新的重要工具，也為面臨艱難診斷的家庭帶來了新的希望。

quiz.question: According to the clinical trial results mentioned in the article, how did the survival time of patients taking the new drug compare to those receiving traditional chemotherapy?

options.B: It was nearly twice as long as the survival time of chemotherapy patients.
options.C: It resulted in a 50% increase in the five-year survival rate.
options.D: It allowed patients to live for a median of 6.7 months more than the previous average.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，服用新藥的患者存活期中位數為 13.2 個月，而傳統化療僅為 6.7 個月，這意味著存活時間幾乎翻倍。選項 A 錯誤，因為 13.2 減去 6.7 為 6.5，而非 6.7。選項 C 混淆了存活時間與五年存活率的概念。選項 D 誤解了數據的比較基準，文中並未提到「先前平均值」的具體數字。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the FDA's decision to allow patient access to the drug before its official approval?

options.A: The FDA was pressured by pharmaceutical companies to bypass safety regulations.
options.B: The drug had already been proven to be a permanent cure for pancreatic cancer.
options.C: Public interest and the severity of the disease influenced the FDA to expedite availability.
options.D: The FDA decided that the drug was safe enough to replace all existing chemotherapy treatments.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第二段，FDA 在正式核准前就允許部分患者使用，是因為該藥物受到高度公眾關注（如前參議員 Ben Sasse 的經驗分享），且 FDA 有義務盡快提供治療。選項 A 文中未提及施壓。選項 B 錯誤，因為第六段明確指出這並非「治癒」。選項 D 過度推論，文中僅提到該藥是新選擇，並未說要完全取代化療。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, the author states that the approval of the drug has 'opened doors' for many other companies. What does 'opened doors' mean in this context?

options.A: It physically allowed company representatives to enter research facilities.
options.B: It created new opportunities for further research and development.
options.C: It forced other companies to lower their prices to stay competitive.
options.D: It resulted in the immediate removal of legal barriers for all cancer drugs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。「Opened doors」在此處為隱喻用法，意指創造了新的可能性或機會。根據上下文，這指的是該藥物的成功促使其他公司開始進行相關的臨床試驗。選項 A 是字面意思，錯誤。選項 C 文中未提及價格競爭。選項 D 過於誇大，僅指該技術領域的發展，而非移除所有藥物的法律門檻。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: To provide a detailed financial breakdown of the pharmaceutical industry's pricing strategies.
options.B: To warn patients about the severe side effects of the new drug Rasonque.
options.C: To explain the biological process of how cancer cells grow in the human body.
options.D: To report on the approval of a promising new pancreatic cancer treatment and its potential impact.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。本文主要報導了 FDA 核准新藥 Rasonque 的新聞，並討論了其臨床數據、對醫療界的意義以及對未來的展望，這是文章的核心主旨。選項 A 僅是文中提到的一個細節。選項 B 錯誤，文章雖提到副作用，但並非警告，而是平衡報導。選項 C 僅是背景知識，並非文章報導的主要目的。
